name: Murder at the Manor
description: A guest lies dead at the manor. Each suspect was in a different room with a different motive. Work out whodunit.
clues: Jealousy goes with at least one of Blackwood or Walking.
Either Crane goes with Revenge, or Grimsby goes with Bathing — but not both.
Between Blackwood and Fairfax, one goes with Envy and the other with Secrecy.
Inheritance goes with at least one of Grimsby, Cooking, or Walking.
Either Cooking goes with Jealousy or Blackwood goes with Cooking.
If Inheritance does not go with Walking, then either Writing goes with Fairfax or Cooking does not go with Blackwood (but not both).
Crane, Fairfax, and Grimsby go with Envy, Inheritance, and Revenge, in some order.

hints.text: Suppose Blackwood went with Jealousy — following the clues from there hits a contradiction, so it doesn't.
chain: Start by assuming Blackwood goes with Jealousy.
Blackwood goes with Jealousy, so it can't also go with Envy.
Blackwood goes with Jealousy, so it can't also go with Secrecy.
…but now the clue “Between Blackwood and Fairfax, one goes with Envy and the other with Secrecy” can no longer hold — a contradiction.
So Blackwood does not go with Jealousy.
